files.description: The architecture of record: widget, bloc, helper, Hive and Firestore layering; bloc and UI-consumer conventions; the offline-first data layer, Freezed/Hive model pairs and the Hive typeId registry; case-participation scoping; lifecycle; roles as custom claims; the standing rules (section 15) and the watchlist of known gaps (section 16). Most questions about why the app is shaped the way it is are answered here.

How a change ships: the CRQ rule, the certification gate (code is committed only after the author has run it), the definition of done, and the P1-P4 severity scale, where breaking a clinical-safety rule is always P1. Also the org: one engineer plus Greptile as the second approver.

The clinical-safety rules S-1 to S-7 and the security threats T-1 to T-16, each with its control and the test that proves it. Check any rules, functions, AI-service or result/alert change against these before treating it as self-contained.

The one service that calls a model: the pre-read pipeline (segment, classify, measure, draft, rank), the rule that every reported number is computed in code, confidence, signing, the Firestore contract for cases/{caseUid}/preread, the standard-endpoint-only policy and cost controls.

Tag, record, detect, draft, approve, deliver. What a notifiable event may contain (and what must never leave a case), the immediate and baseline detector rules, approval as a callable, two-phase delivery, and the rule that patients choose a county and are never located.

The Local-versus-Cloud rule, the notifications collection being server-written only, the three idempotency guards, lock-screen-safe push copy that never names a diagnosis, and template-based localisation.

Semantic color roles, Manrope throughout and which TextTheme slot takes which, the 4-point AppSpacing scale, and the clinical UI conventions: unsigned AI output always inside AiDraftFrame, confidence and urgency never conveyed by color alone, the viewer and patient copy rules.
The test layers (unit and bloc, widget at 1.0x and 2.0x text scale in en and sw, rules, model evaluation, UAT) and when a UAT or EVAL report is due.
